meeting_header:
Date: 2026-10-05
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Alvarez (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Lyra VP Partnerships), Derek Mills (Lyra Head of Solutions), Nora Kim (Lyra Partnerships Ops)
summary: Partner GTM orchestration meeting focused on a stalled co-sell opportunity in EMEA. Discussion covered deal blockers (pricing credits, technical pilot constraints, SSO/VPC requirements), a quick benchmark ask, and next steps to unblock the pilot. Action items assigned to both Redwood and Lyra owners.
topics: status of the stalled EMEA pilot opportunity
technical feasibility: VPC/on-prem vs hosted and audit logs
hand-off process and joint customer intro
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): All right folks, thanks for joining. I think we have about 55 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Anika (Lyra): Hi everyone, Anika here.
[00:08] Derek (Lyra): Derek here.
[00:09] Nora (Lyra): Nora on the line.
[00:11] Miguel (Redwood): Miguel, SE.
[00:13] Sofia (Redwood): Great, cool. Goal for today — we want to figure out where the EMEA pilot sits, the stall reasons, and what immediate artifacts or tests will move this forward. Anika, can you kick off with the current state?
[00:27] Anika (Lyra): Yeah, sure. So quick background — we've been working a lead for a mid-sized retailer in the UK. They want an LLM-powered merch recommender widget. We introduced Redwood via our integration partner SomeEdge, they liked the speed in your demo but procurement pushed on pricing and audit. It's kind of in limbo.
[00:45] Sofia (Redwood): Understood. When you say procurement pushed on audit, is that SOC 2 plus data residency or are they asking for infra-level controls?
[00:53] Anika (Lyra): Both actually. They want SOC 2 Type II evidence, SSO with SAML, and worried about tokens leaving the EU. They asked whether Redwood can run in their VPC or on-prem.
[01:05] Miguel (Redwood): Quick clarification — our Redwood Private option supports VPC-hosted control plane and can be deployed on customer-managed infra. We can do KMS integration for key control. The on-prem pack we have is air-gapped compatible but that usually needs a longer procurement window.
[01:22] Derek (Lyra): That makes sense. The timing is the main issue — they want a pilot in six weeks. Air-gapped on-prem is likely too slow. They were hoping for a VPC-hosted option that still meets EU residency and audit logs.
[01:36] Sofia (Redwood): So probably Redwood Dedicated or Private VPC is the sweet spot — predictable latency and ability to route regionally. Miguel, any quick notes on latency expected in EMEA region with our dedicated pools?
[01:47] Miguel (Redwood): For the model variant we demoed — p50 around 60–80 ms for generation (short prompts), p95 around 250–400 ms depending on sequence length. Those are ballpark; we should run a pilot bench with their typical prompt mix.
[02:03] Nora (Lyra): Two follow-ups — 1) pricing: our partner team needs a clear partner crediting if we bring a lead. 2) technical: can you provide an artifact that shows redwood's audit logs and how long logs are retained?
[02:16] Sofia (Redwood): Yes, we'll send a partner pricing overlay and a security pack. For logs, we can provide a redwood-infra audit export example and details on retention policies. Note sometimes the auto-transcription of docs calls our KV cache 'K V cash' in some examples — please ignore that, sorry.
[02:35] Derek (Lyra): Laughs. Okay. Pricing is the immediate blocker — procurement said the list price with a 15% margin is too high for their pilot budget. They asked whether Lyra could get a channel credit or deal registration discount.
[02:49] Sofia (Redwood): We have standard partner credits for channel-sourced deals; amount varies by commit and ARR. Anika/Nora, do you have an internal expectation for the credit level?
[03:00] Anika (Lyra): We typically aim for 20% credit for sourced pilots under 6 months. If Redwood can commit to a similar range, procurement warms up. If not, we might need to co-fund the pilot.
[03:12] Miguel (Redwood): Also worth noting total cost is heavily dependent on batching and caching. If their workload is consistent we can suggest quantization model presets and batching params that shave token cost by 30% or more. That could help procurement's math.
[03:26] Derek (Lyra): Are those changes quick to implement? Pilot timeline is tight.
[03:29] Miguel (Redwood): Some are config changes we can do in hours (batch sizing, prefix cache). Quantization profile changes might take a day or two for verification. But we can deploy a conservative config rapidly.
[03:40] Sofia (Redwood): Right — pragmatic approach: 1) pricing overlay + channel credits, 2) a short perf bench using their sample prompts (we can do a single-run quick test), 3) security docs to unblock procurement. That should address their top three asks.
[03:56] Nora (Lyra): On the security docs, procurement specifically asked about export controls and where tokens might be logged. Do you have a short diagram of control plane vs data plane?
[04:06] Miguel (Redwood): Yep, we have a standard diagram. Data plane for inference stays in customer's chosen region when using Private or Dedicated; hosted default keeps data in nearest region but not guaranteed for EEA residency unless specified. We'll send the diagram.
[04:22] Anika (Lyra): One twist — SomeEdge has been pushing their bundled offering which includes their own caching layer. Procurement thinks moving to SomeEdge end-to-end is lower risk because of an existing relationship. We want Redwood to provide a compelling technical and commercial package to win the joint lead.
[04:40] Sofia (Redwood): Understood. I'd like to propose a small joint proof-of-concept where Redwood runs the inference and SomeEdge handles the front-end integration. That way the retailer sees end-to-end latency and integration burden. Would Lyra and SomeEdge be comfortable?
[04:53] Derek (Lyra): Likely yes, provided the integration responsibilities and credits are clear. This is where the partner crediting docs matter.
[05:02] Sofia (Redwood): Cool. Miguel, can you outline the bench we should run for procurement?
[05:06] Miguel (Redwood): I'd run three things: 1) synthetic head-to-head using their typical prompt mix vs Anthropic (if they requested), 2) end-to-end from front-end through SomeEdge and Redwood to measure real user latency, and 3) cost projection over a 6-week pilot with estimated tokens per session. For the synthetic we record p50/p95/p99 and token cost delta.
[05:26] Anika (Lyra): They specifically asked for p99 numbers, that's what procurement cares about for SLAs.
[05:30] Miguel (Redwood): We'll include p99. Quick caveat — synthetic p99 can be noisy; best to run repeated passes. We'll do at least 3 runs and aggregate.
[05:40] Nora (Lyra): On the contract side — we need to know if Redwood's standard MSA supports partner-sourced credits and references to channel lead registration.
[05:49] Sofia (Redwood): Yes, our MSA has partner clauses; I'll check the exact language and pull a redlined example. If needed, legal can fast-track a simple amendment for a pilot.
[05:58] Derek (Lyra): Okay good. Timeline-wise, if we get pricing and security docs by Friday (Oct 8), procurement can meet next week. That align with your timeline?
[06:10] Sofia (Redwood): Yes, we'll prioritize. Miguel, will bench be done by Monday-Tuesday?
[06:15] Miguel (Redwood): I can start runs Monday and have preliminary numbers by EOD Tuesday. I'll need the sample prompt set and a small dataset from Lyra/the retailer.
[06:23] Anika (Lyra): We'll share a sanitized sample prompt set and session distribution by Friday.
[06:27] Derek (Lyra): Note — they also asked about observability: per-route token breakdowns, tracing, and cost per token by user segment. Is that exposed?
[06:36] Miguel (Redwood): Our Console exposes token-level breakdowns and per-route dashboards. We can give you a screenshot and a short explainer. In Private/Dedicated we can also enable longer retention for logs.
[06:46] Anika (Lyra): Great. Any red flags we should surface now — things that would make this a no-go?
[06:51] Miguel (Redwood): If they absolutely require air-gapped on-prem inside six weeks, that's a likely no-go. Also if they demand changes to model weights or host custom training in pilot, that becomes a different project.
[07:02] Sofia (Redwood): Noted. But sounds like feasible otherwise. Let's talk crediting mechanics briefly — Nora, can you describe how Lyra typically books partner revenue and how credits get applied?
[07:13] Nora (Lyra): We usually do a partner-sourced registration. If a partner sources the deal, we provide a 20% rebate on usage for the pilot. For larger commitments there are tiered credits. The issue is sometimes the ISV (like SomeEdge) expects a channel fee too, so we need split model clarity.
[07:31] Sofia (Redwood): We can support split credits — we just need the registration docs. I'll draft a template so it doesn't get delayed by legal.
[07:40] Anika (Lyra): Perfect.
[07:42] Miguel (Redwood): Quick technical note: caching prefix/KV cache can reduce calls for repeat sessions. If SomeEdge keeps a short-term cache at the edge, that significantly improves p50 but p99 remains dominated by cold-starts or long sequences. We can experiment with TTLs.
[07:56] Derek (Lyra): That makes sense. For the retailer, cold-start p99 is the pain point. They want to guarantee sub-600 ms p99 for interactive sessions.
[08:06] Miguel (Redwood): Sub-600 ms p99 is achievable in region with Dedicated GPUs for the specific model size we tested; need to validate with their exact prompt length distribution.
[08:16] Sofia (Redwood): Okay — action plan recap so far: Redwood sends partner pricing overlay + MSA excerpt + security pack; Lyra shares sanitized prompts and comp matrix; Miguel runs bench and returns p50/p95/p99 and cost delta. Any other critical asks?
[08:33] Anika (Lyra): Can you also include an example of a canary/fallback policy? Procurement worries about graceful degradation if a model fails.
[08:41] Miguel (Redwood): Yes, we have routing policies — we can show a canary that falls back to a cheaper model variant or a cached response. I'll include a short YAML snippet as an example, though the procurement folks might not read YAML but it's useful for engineering.
[08:58] Derek (Lyra): On the commercial side, are there minimum commits for Dedicated? Procurement is worried we'll be forced into a larger commit for the credits.
[09:08] Sofia (Redwood): Dedicated has commit levels, but we can structure a pilot as a reserved short-term capacity or a usage agreement with credit back. I'll outline options in the pricing overlay.
[09:19] Nora (Lyra): One procedural ask — when we do the joint intro to the retailer, Lyra wants Redwood and SomeEdge on the call. Can Redwood also bring a short technical win-story deck (1-2 slides) and a quick runbook?
[09:32] Sofia (Redwood): Absolutely. We'll prepare a 2-slide technical summary and a one-page runbook with integration roles.
[09:39] Anika (Lyra): Awesome. A small nit — procurement wants to see incident response SLAs and access to audit logs for 90 days. Is that standard?
[09:48] Miguel (Redwood): 90-day retention is fine for Dedicated/Private. For hosted we have standard retention shorter but can be extended as an add-on. We'll document that.
[09:58] Sofia (Redwood): Great. Anything else before we go into blockers and how to handle the SomeEdge competition?
[10:05] Derek (Lyra): Yes — SomeEdge pitched being the one-stop vendor and said they could host both front-end and inference in their managed offering. The retailer likes one throat to choke. We need to position Redwood as the best inference partner while enabling SomeEdge integration.
[10:21] Sofia (Redwood): So joint-sell play: Redwood provides the inference SLA + security pack, SomeEdge provides front-end integration and edge caching. Lyra coordinates. We propose a co-sell credit and a simple runbook that clarifies support boundaries. If SomeEdge insists on exclusivity, that complicates things.
[10:36] Anika (Lyra): SomeEdge is not asking for exclusivity, but they want priority. We'll try to make priority work if credits and responsibilities are clear.
[10:44] Miguel (Redwood): Also, small note — Anthropic mentioned by procurement as a benchmark on cost/accuracy — if you want a head-to-head we'll need credentials for Anthropic or we can use public demos. It helps if the retail team's typical prompt set is shared.
[10:57] Nora (Lyra): We'll request permission from the retailer to run a controlled benchmark. If they approve, we'll push sample prompts to you.
[11:05] Sofia (Redwood): Excellent. Any risks we should put on the table?
[11:08] Derek (Lyra): Timing — six weeks to pilot is tight; procurement cycles can slip.
[11:12] Miguel (Redwood): Technical risk — if the retailer requires custom model fine-tuning, that's out of scope for a quick pilot.
[11:17] Anika (Lyra): Commercial risk — if credits don't land, Lyra can't justify co-funding and will not push the lead.
[11:22] Sofia (Redwood): Acknowledged. Let's set deadlines: security & pricing doc by Friday Oct 8; Lyra sends prompts and comp matrix by Friday Oct 8; Miguel bench by Tue Oct 13 (prelim) — is everyone ok?
[11:36] Derek (Lyra): Slight correction — earlier Miguel said EOD Tuesday (Oct 9) but internal calendar suggests Tue the 13th is safer. Can we aim for preliminary by Oct 9 and a verification run by Oct 13?
[11:48] Miguel (Redwood): Yes, preliminary by Oct 9 if they provide prompts Friday. We'll run more exhaustive runs by the 13th.
[11:55] Nora (Lyra): Sounds good. Also, we'll schedule a joint intro to the retailer for week of Oct 12 — I'll propose times after procurement confirms.
[12:05] Sofia (Redwood): Perfect. Any final questions?
[12:09] Anika (Lyra): One last ask — can Redwood provide a short case about a retailer or commerce customer with similar latency requirements? A 1-paragraph reference would help procurement.
[12:18] Sofia (Redwood): I'll share a redacted reference paragraph and customer win blurb.
[12:22] Derek (Lyra): Thanks.
[12:24] Sofia (Redwood): Okay — recap: pricing + credit language, security pack + audit diagram, run the perf bench, prepare two-slide tech deck and a runbook, coordinate joint intro. We'll follow up with the deck and docs by Friday. I'll email the pricing overlay after this call.
[12:40] Miguel (Redwood): I'll put the bench plan in an internal sheet and share read-only with Anika/Nora.
[12:46] Nora (Lyra): Thanks, Miguel.
[12:48] Sofia (Redwood): Great, thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after the bench results and procurement feedback.
[12:54] Call ends with quick goodbye exchange and some crosstalk about scheduling.
notes: Customer is leaning toward VPC-hosted pilot to meet EU residency
SomeEdge is competing as integrated vendor; joint-sell path preferred
Procurement wants p99 and audit docs; pricing is main blocker
